post.caption: Two tiny gold men stitch a fleece. It is a gold collar from the 4th century BC. On 21 June 1971, archaeologist Borys Mozolevsky found it in a burial mound in Ukraine. It weighs about 2.5 pounds and is about 12 inches wide. Four twisted gold tubes frame three bands of scenes: a cow and calf and a horse and foal on top, a gold plant with five birds in the middle, and fighting animals at the bottom. About 50 tiny cast gold figures fill it. It belongs to the National Museum of the History of Ukraine in Kyiv.
